disposition.reason: A neighbor appealed the Burlington ZBA's affirmance of the Zoning Administrator's refusal to take enforcement action against seven students renting an existing single-family house. It is a municipal appeal, but it concerns occupancy of an existing house without construction, which is not new housing.

evidence.quote: Appellant John Mentes appealed from the May 31, 2000 decision of the then-Zoning Board of Adjustment (ZBA) of the City of Burlington
affirming the Zoning Administrator= s decision not to take enforcement action1 against Appellees Charles and Cynthia Burns
Appellees own a seven-bedroom single-family residence at 36 North Willard Street
Appellees rented the house as a whole, that is, not divided into separate apartments or rented out as separate rooms, to seven students
the shared student housing use of Appellees= house is prohibited under the 1999 ordinance, concludes the above-captioned appeal.

judgments.note: Appeal of a ZBA decision upholding the refusal to enforce against students renting an existing house; GUIDE's table treats rooms let to students or change of occupancy without construction as not new housing, so excluded.
The docket appeals the City of Burlington ZBA's May 31, 2000 decision.
Existing seven-bedroom house; dispute is only whether occupancy by seven unrelated students is permitted. No construction or new units.

history.note: Excluded: enforcement appeal over student occupancy of an existing house, not new housing.
